newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close down slightly in trendless mkt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close down slightly in trendless mkt.

text.p: Brazil stocks closed slightly lower in moderate trade, despite sharp rises in electrical sector shares, with many investors simply rolling over positions, brokers said.
"Market has no firm trend. Players will only define a trend a few days before options settlements" on Oct 21, one trader said.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares shed 44 points to close at 66,267 points, down 0.07 percent, on turnover of 381 million reais ($370.4 million).
On Friday, the market will be eyeing Wall Street's performance due to a lack of fresh developments on the domestic side.
Power firms' shares were again big winners. The Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index rose 1.84 percent to end at 1,724 points.

Minas Gerais state power firm Cemig common shares soared 9.3 percent to close at 43.50 reais on heavy foreign buying due to unconfirmed rumors that the state would sell a third of the firm's voting stock to a Chilean firm.
The preferred share ended at 33.90 reais, up 3.04 percent. Minas Gerais is slated to auction a 33 percent stake in Cemig in December.
Federal power company Eletrobras preferred shares rose 1.28 percent and closed at 317 reais.
Benchmark Telebras preferred stock dropped 0.37 percent to end at 81.30 reais.
